title: The tumour-derived extracellular vesicle proteome varies by endometrial cancer histology and is confounded by an obesogenic environment
projectDescription: Endometrial cancer is the most prevalent gynaecological cancer globally. Its association with obesity and metabolic diseases is a key aetiology, increasingly among younger females. Early diagnosis and improved treatment decisions are crucial for these individuals which could be fulfilled by the discovery of new biomarkers.  We took a new approach to extracellular vesicle (EV) biomarker discovery - profiling the proteome of enriched EVs isolated directly from frozen biobanked endometrial cancers. Nine tissue pools, each generating collagenase-digested tissue and matched small EVs, were analysed using label-free proteomics. Three clinical subgroups: Endometrioid low BMI (body mass index), Endometrioid high BMI, and Serous, irrespective of BMI were compared to identify shared secreted proteins, proteins associated with histological subtype, and proteins related to BMI. EVs were enriched for common EV markers and large secreted proteins. Cell lysates were enriched in mitochondrial and blood proteins. EV protein profiles were most different between the high BMI subgroup and the others, highlighting a significant influence of co-morbidities on the intra-tumoural EV secretome. Proteins that were differentially abundant between subgroups in tissues, were strikingly not also differential in the matched EVs. This work has identified secreted proteins implicated in the complex pathophysiology of endometrial cancer and pinpointed candidate biomarkers for diagnosis.
sampleProcessingProtocol: EVs were enriched from tumour tissues using the protocol established previously, with minor modifications. Frozen tumour tissues were dissected lengthways on prechilled plastic plate into 2-3 mm wide sections, weighed and samples pooled to achieve >150 mg each. Samples were digested with 50U/mL of collagenase type 3 (Worthington LS004180) in PBS (8 µL per 1 mg of tissue). A collagenase-based method was selected to maintain surface epitopes on the EVs. Samples were incubated in a shaking water bath at 25°C for 20 min. During this incubation, the tube was mixed by inversion at the 5 min mark and gently pipetted twice at 10 min. Following the incubation, the tube was placed on ice and PhosSTOP and Complete Protease Inhibitor (Sigma-Aldrich) were added to a final concentration of 1 —. Dissociated tissues were pelleted at 300 g for 5 min at 4°C and supernatant retained. An aliquot (~30 mg) of the pellet in 570 µL PBS, was homogenised using a MICCRA D-9 cell homogeniser for 10 sec at 50% intensity, and sonicated (Transsonic T460/H, Lab-Line) on ice for 20 min ("collagenase digested tissue", TC). Homogenised lysates were then repelleted at 10,000 xg for 5 min at 4°C to remove debris, and cleared lysate transferred into new tubes and stored at -80°C. The supernatant from the initial 300 xg centrifugation was transferred to a new tube, spun at 2000 xg for 10 min at 4°C, followed by centrifugation at 10,000 xg for 30 min at 4Â°C to pellet large EVs (Mi). The supernatant in 10mL PBS was applied onto a qEV10/ 35 nm legacy column (IZON Science) for size exclusion chromatography (SEC) purification using an Automated Fraction Collector (IZON Science) following the manufacturer's protocol. The first 20 mL flow through were discarded (void volume). Subsequent fractions 1 to 3 (20 mL each) were individually concentrated with Amicon Ultra-15 centrifuge filters (10 kDa, Merck) by spinning at 4000 xg at 4°C to a volume of ~600-1000 µL to yield small EVs (sEV) and stored at -80°C. SEC was selected, rather than Density Gradient Ultracentrifugation to maximise EV yields, acknowledging that fine separation of different density EV subsets is not feasible using SEC.
dataProcessingProtocol: The DIA-NN was used for the Swath data quantification [21]. The constructed spectral library was converted to the DIA-NN compatible library via the Fragpipe [22]. The match-between-runs method was selected to produce more consistent quantification result. The normalization at the injection level was disabled. The mass accuracy was automatically estimated using the first run in the experiment. Cross-run analysis was conducted to generate the global q-values for protein and gene groups. Output was filtered at 0.01 FDR  for precursors and protein/gene groups. A report spectral library  was re-assembled from the first pass result. The mass accuracy and RT window were re-estimated using the runs in the experiment. The peaks were picked and integrated in a double-pass mode of Neural network classifier.   In order to enhance clarity, we employed the gene names that corresponded to the proteins of interest.
